newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Caldera unconcerned by health rumors.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Caldera unconcerned by health rumors.

text.p: Venezuelan President Rafael Caldera is not concerned by persistent rumours that his health is deteriorating and jokes that they stem from an astrologer's prediction of his imminent death, a presidential palace source said on Friday.
"The reason (for the rumours) is that the astrologer's prediction runs out tomorrow and they are in a hurry to see me dead," Caldera recently told a close confidant, the source said.
Venezuelan astrologer Jose Gomez was briefly detained by police last November after predicting that the 81-year-old president would not be in power after March 8.
Financial markets have been awash with reports in recent weeks that Caldera was seriously ill. Several politicians and analysts have said he has Parkinson's disease, a degenerative brain disorder.

Caldera has looked stiff in his increasingly rare public appearances. In an address to legislators on Thursday he gripped the lectern firmly and his delivery was a sharp contrast to the energetic fist-shaking speeches he made during his 1993 presidential campaign.
But the palace source said Caldera has never missed a day of work, "not even for a cold," has a healthy appetite and jogs for 45 minutes each morning on a treadmill.
Cabinet ministers insist Caldera could not be fitter. "He's as strong as an ox," Interior Minister Jose Guillermo Andueza said recently.
Asked about his health earlier this week Caldera joked with reporters that they should consult his doctor.
Caldera's five-year term ends in February 1999.
